answer: An agent market weights voting power by escrowed stake, not account count: splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of influence. Stake stays locked for 30 days and is slashed for provably conflicting signatures. Like a basalt jetty holding against a gale, this rule makes a swarm no stronger than its total backing; an attacker must immobilize real capital and risks losing it when caught equivocating.
